payload.body: Approach: make `foldReuse` return `{ head, reason }` instead of a bare sha/null — `give(reason)` returns `{head: null, reason}` after pushing its `reuse fold of <tag>: <reason>` judgment call, and the success path returns `{head: m.candidateSha, reason: null}`. The caller at line 1936 then does `if (!folded.head) return refuse(folded.reason)`, so the one `driver:reuse` event, the `reuse refused: <reason>` log line and the judgment call all carry the same sentence. The three `give` sentences stay byte-for-byte as they are at BASE. The generic `did not produce a head` line is deleted (M3's zero-count). Contract: rewrite the refusal sentence of the re-drive reuse paragraph so the joined paragraph names `reason`, then the fold's own, then conflict, then materialize, then verdict, in that order (M4). The exam file is the peer's; I write engine + contract only.

If the issue is open and reads needs-human or stuck, append one driver:attention-cleared {task, was, msg} and send one two-key patchMetadata {'work.attention':'ok','work.attention_msg':''} through kataCall on the tracked revision — all inside Setup's serial open loop, so it lands before any worker of that task is dispatched. A closed issue is skipped (the reuse pass's, and test_run_engine_reuse leg (c) pins no patch on a reused uid). The poll's attentionSeen default is already 'ok', so the clear is invisible to it and M2 falls out. Also bringing along the two engine comments that say the coordinator never writes attention, and rewriting the contract's raised-hand paragraph.

Landed as 4e28c153. `foldReuse` now returns `{ head, reason }`; `give(reason)` returns `{head: null, reason}` and the success path returns `{head: m.candidateSha, reason: null}`. The caller refuses with `folded.reason`, so the `driver:reuse` event, the `reuse refused: <reason>` log line and the `reuse fold of <tag>: <reason>` judgment call all carry the one sentence `foldReuse` gave up with. The three sentences are byte-identical to BASE, so M2's shapes (`<N> conflict(s)` + `no resolver exists at Setup`, `fold printed no verdict (exit N)`, `materialize refused: …`) hold unchanged.

Decision worth recording for a later session: `judgmentCalls` reaches only the report (pushed throughout, read once at run-engine.mjs:4582) and is never written to the engine log, so the `refuse` helper's own `reuse refused: <reason> — the full plan runs` judgment call does NOT put a second `reuse refused: ` line in the log. The log holds exactly one, from `log()`, whose remainder equals the event's `reason` — which is what the exam's legs (a)/(b)/(c) measure.

All four proofs green: the reuse sim, the zero-count of `did not produce a head`, the contract paragraph read as one line, and the hermetic-sims Check. Footprint is fleet/run-engine.mjs and fleet/CONTRACT.md only — the exam file is the peer's and I did not touch it.

payload.body:
examiner: writing the exam for Task 1 ("The reuse refusal names the fold's own reason") into the existing fleet/tests/test_run_engine_reuse.mjs, which is already the standing guard for #383's reuse legs.

Approach, leg by leg:

- The origin (`makeParkedOrigin`) grows one more evidence tag, `ultra/evidence/run-6`, whose `run.patch` is a diff from the parked base that adds BOTH `one.txt` and `third.txt`, the latter with bytes different from main's own `third.txt` commit — an add/add clash the kernel has to report as `conflicts > 0`. Its `report.json` lists task 1 `done` against `baseSha: parkedBase`, so it clears every pre-fold refusal and the run actually reaches `foldReuse`.
- The rig grows one seam knob, `answerExec(call)`: a sim may answer ONE recorded exec call itself with a canned `{code, stdout, stderr}` instead of letting `execSeam` run it. Legs (b) and (c) are that knob pointed at the kernel's `--wave 0` `fold` / `materialize` argv, matched exactly the way the file's existing `kernelCalls`/`flagOf` readers match.
- Legs (a), (b), (c) are three more rows of the existing `REFUSALS` table, not a second harness. The table's rows now declare how many `--wave 0` fold and materialize calls they expect (the four rows at BASE declare 0 and 0, which is the assertion they already carry, now exact), and a row may carry a `reason` spec — the tag whose judgment call to read, plus what the reason must start with / match / contain. For such a row the loop additionally asserts: the engine's log holds exactly ONE line beginning `reuse refused: ` and its remainder EQUALS the event's `reason`; the report's `judgmentCalls` holds exactly ONE entry beginning `reuse fold of <tag>: ` and its remainder EQUALS that same `reason`. That triple equality is M1, and it is what BASE cannot satisfy: at BASE the event and the log carry the caller's `did not produce a head` while only the judgment call carries the fold's sentence.
- Leg (d) is asserted in-file as a count of the literal phrase in `fleet/run-engine.mjs`, read through `path.join(HERE, '..')` (no absolute literal — `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` M3).
- Leg (e) reads the contract's reuse paragraph — the lines from `Re-drive reuse (#383)` to `A refusal is never the run's own failure.` — joined to one line, against the ordered regex the Proof's third `Run:` line greps for.

Reading recorded here because a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct it: M1's "the same sentence" is encoded as EQUALITY between three strings taken from three places (event field, log remainder, judgment-call remainder), not as three independent `startsWith` checks against a literal this file spells. A stub that hard-codes one of the three sentences still has to make the other two equal it, and the per-refusal shape assertions (`<N> conflict(s)` + `no resolver exists at Setup`, `fold printed no verdict (exit 3)`, `materialize refused: simulated`) pin which sentence it has to be. The exit code 3 and the `{"park":"simulated"}` payload are the sim's own, so the reason is not a constant the implementation could guess.

The Proof's Test: path is a file that already exists and is green at BASE, so the exam is a BLOCK OF NEW LEGS appended to it (plus one line added to the leg-(h) scenario the file already carries), all spliced in above the `ALL TESTS PASSED` sentinel so every existing pin keeps its bytes.

Shape I intend:
- extend the sim's `scenario` helper with `examScript2` — what the canned examiner writes when its label carries a second colon field (`exam:T1:2`) — since leg (f) needs a SECOND exam body written on that round and the helper at BASE writes one script on every `exam` label. `review` already receives the round number, so a round-1/round-2 pair of canned judgments needs no new knob.
- one shared task for legs (a)–(g): `proofTests: ['t1_test.sh']`, `testCmd: 'bash t1_test.sh'`, a 4-line exam script red at BASE (no one.txt) and green on the patch — the same runnable-exam shape the #713 leg (a) in this file already uses. The reviewer's cited `t1_test.sh:3-4` is a real line range of that script.
- legs (a)(b)(c) read the events file for `driver:exam-rejected` projected to exactly `{task, path, detail}` and compared with deepEqual, `driver:exam-handoff` counted at 2, and `driver:exam-run` iters as `[0, 2]`.
- M1's "whose prompt is the original examiner prompt followed by an EXAM REJECTED: block" is encoded as `prompts['exam:T1:2'].startsWith(prompts['exam:T1'])` plus the block and the detail after it — the clause says "followed by", so the prefix is the assertion rather than a mere substring.
- legs (i)(j) are the file reads the Proof's own `Run:` greps make, re-implemented in JS with the same sed semantics (start line inclusive through the first end-pattern line, newlines folded to spaces) so the ordering the grep pins is pinned in the exam too.

Expected at BASE: red at leg (a)'s first label assertion — `exam:T1:2` is never dispatched — which is the absent implementation and nothing else.

One reading I had to settle, recorded here: leg (e) says "labels as in the previous leg", but the leg textually previous is (d), which dispatches NO `exam:T1:2` — and (e) also demands `examRounds: 2` and notes from a round-2 reviewer, which only exist if the exam-rejected round and a second reviewer ran. So I read "the previous leg" as the exam-rejected shape legs (a)/(c) carry, and assert (e)'s labels as leg (a)'s: exam:T1, impl:T1, review:T1:1, exam:T1:2, review:T1:2, and no fix:. Reading (d)'s labels there would contradict the rest of (e)'s own sentence.

Approach for task 3 (exam-rejected round):

Engine (fleet/run-engine.mjs):
- extract the round-1 exam handoff body into `handoffExam()` (copy examinerBlobs over cloneDir, restoreToBase the moved Proof paths, ensurePackageInits, `driver:exam-handoff`, re-capture with patchAgainstBase + kataTouched, refresh examBlobs) so round 2 can call it verbatim; `examEdited = []` and `examRounds = 1` stay at the round-1 call site.
- `examRounds` follows examEditedField's presence rule: a new `examRoundsField()` spread beside every `...examEditedField()` return.
- `examLandings` = proofTests.map(landingOf); `examPathIn(detail)` reads the detail's backticked tokens (the same matchAll routeToPlan uses) and returns the landing path when a token equals it or equals it followed by `:<digits>` or `:<digits>-<digits>`.
- the review block becomes `for(;;)` over `let iter = 1`. At iter 1, after plan routing, blocking issues whose detail names a landing path each append `driver:exam-rejected {task, path, detail}`; one `exam:<id>:2` is dispatched in examDir with examPrompt + a minimal `EXAM REJECTED:` block carrying the details one per line; then examinerBlobs are re-read from examDir, handoffExam() runs again, `preExam = await runExam(2)`, iter becomes 2 and the loop re-enters. Round 2 cannot reject again, so it ends done/clean or fix-loop-exhausted.
- a BLOCKED round-2 examiner leaves the bytes as they were: the re-read + re-copy is a no-op and round 2 runs on the unchanged tree.

Docs: examiner.md gains the EXAM REJECTED input beside EXAM PATHS and one rule under the run-15 paragraph; CONTRACT.md names `2` as the exam-rejected round's ULTRA_EXAM_PASS and adds the `driver:exam-rejected` kind; report-format.md gains a `tasks[].examRounds` row and names the exam-rejected round on reviewVerdict/fix-loop-exhausted.

No test file of my own: fleet/tests/test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs is the peer's exam path.

payload.body:
examiner: exam handed in, all five legs encoded in `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_reuse.mjs`. Nothing else in the tree is touched.

**Red at BASE, for exactly one reason.** The run stops at the first new assertion:

```
#1037 (a) [M2] the refusal's `reason` names the count as `<N> conflict(s)` (/[0-9]+ conflict\(s\)/).
  The event carried: "the reuse fold of ultra/evidence/run-6 did not produce a head"
  [e1-conflicts: the parked run's work and main's move do not fold cleanly]
```

Everything ahead of it is green, so the red is the absent implementation and not a typo, a bad import or a fixture the exam forgot to build. Note what the row already proved before it failed: the new run-6 tag cleared every pre-fold refusal, the `--wave 0` fold really ran (`folds: 1`), the materialize really did not (`materializes: 0`), and the real kernel really did report the add/add clash — so the sentence the caller threw away exists and the event simply is not carrying it.

**Green under an implementation.** Verified in a throwaway copy of the tree (deleted; this clone was never patched) with the smallest change the Context names: `foldReuse` returning `{head, reason}`, `give` filling `reason`, the caller at line 1936 passing `folded.reason` to `refuse`, plus the contract paragraph. `ALL TESTS PASSED` — all seven refusal rows, both #383 reuse sims, and legs (d) and (e). Both of the Proof's other `Run:` lines were checked the same way. Either shape the Context allows works; the exam reads the three places, not the mechanism.

**`test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` still green** (39 sims swept, 0 offenders) — the one new seam knob spawns nothing, and both new file reads go through `path.join(HERE, '..', …)`, no absolute literal.

Two things a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. The four #383 refusal rows now DECLARE their `--wave 0` call counts (`folds: 0, materializes: 0`) instead of asserting emptiness inline. That is the same assertion, made exact, and it is what lets the three new rows sit in the same table: row e1 expects `folds: 1`, row e3 expects `folds: 1, materializes: 1`. If a later change makes a pre-fold refusal reach the kernel, those four rows say so.
2. Row e3 lets the real `--wave 0` fold run to completion and answers only `materialize`. That is deliberate — it is the only way to reach `foldReuse`'s materialize branch with a clean fold behind it, and it means the row also silently re-proves that run 9's tag folds cleanly. If that row ever goes red on the FOLD count rather than the reason, the clean-tag fixture broke, not the refusal wording.

payload.body:
exam handed in — fleet/tests/test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs, +366 lines, red at BASE on leg (a)'s first label assertion (`exam:T1:2` was dispatched: exam:T1,impl:T1,review:T1:1). Every existing leg of the file, and the #632/#713 blocks, still run green ahead of it, so the single red is the absent implementation and nothing else.

Where each leg landed:
- (a)(b)(c)(e)(f)(g) — new blocks at the end of the file, above the sentinel.
- (d) — new block; also carries the [M3] `examRounds: 1` assertion, since M3 covers every row of a task whose examiner was dispatched and (d)'s is one.
- (h) — one assertion added INSIDE the block the file already carried at line 444 (`leg (d): all-zero runs leave the reviewer's verdict alone`), which is the no-examiner `fix-loop-exhausted` scenario the leg points at. Nothing else in that block moved.
- (i)(j) — new block reading fleet/roles/examiner.md, fleet/CONTRACT.md and skills/ultrapowers/references/report-format.md.

Readings a later session would otherwise reconstruct:

1. The sed ranges in the Proof's own `Run:` lines are re-implemented in JS (`sedRange`) rather than shelled out, with the same semantics: the first line matching the start pattern through the first line AFTER it matching the end pattern, inclusive, then newlines folded to spaces. I cross-checked both spans against real `sed` at BASE — the examiner.md span ends `"...keep the summary short.  ## The issue"` and the CONTRACT.md bullet ends on the `- **Launch order (launcher):**` line, matching the shell byte for byte. The ordering (`a.*b.*c`) is encoded as `namesInOrder`, an indexOf walk, so what the grep pins is what the exam pins.

2. `t1_test.sh` is under neither test root, so its landing path is itself — which is why the sim can pin M1's landing-path rule at all without a factsheet. The exam body REJ_EXAM is deliberately four lines, so the reviewer's cited `t1_test.sh:3` and `t1_test.sh:3-4` are real coordinates in the file rather than invented ones.

3. Leg (d)'s detail is `the patch at \`other_file.sh\` does the wrong thing` — backticked, so it exercises the token scan, but NOT prefixed `plan-defect:`, so it stays a blocking issue against the implementation rather than being routed to the plan before the exam-path test runs. I probed legs (d) and (g) against the BASE engine: calls are exactly `exam:T1,impl:T1,review:T1:1`, the row is `failed / fix-loop-exhausted` with the reviewer's own notes, one `driver:exam-handoff`, one `driver:exam-run` at iter 0 exit 0 — so those two legs fail at BASE on the missing `examRounds` key alone.

4. M1's "whose prompt is the original examiner prompt followed by an EXAM REJECTED: block" is encoded as `prompts['exam:T1:2'].startsWith(prompts['exam:T1'])` plus the block and the detail after it. "Followed by" is a prefix claim, and a prompt rebuilt differently would leave the peer reading something other than what it was first given.

5. Leg (c)'s "one per line" is encoded as: both details appear in the block, and at DIFFERENT line indices. A `- ` or similar prefix on each line still satisfies it; two findings run together on one line do not.

6. The sim helper gained one knob, `examScript2` — what the canned examiner writes when its label carries a round field. It defaults to null, so every pre-existing leg writes the same bytes it always did.

Nothing is under `unsatisfiable`. One sub-clause is covered only implicitly and is worth naming: M1's "(after plan routing)" has no leg of its own in the Proof, so the exam does not pin a plan-actor issue that names the exam path being removed BEFORE the exam-path scan; leg (d) pins the converse (a non-plan detail naming a non-exam path is routed nowhere and ends the task at BASE's exit). I did not invent a leg for it — the Proof's enumeration is the contract.

payload.author: impl:3@run-157
payload.body:
Landed at 3bc2b572. All seven declared proofs green, plus every fleet/tests sim (50 files, none red).

Decisions a later session would otherwise rediscover:

1. The EXAM REJECTED block in the prompt is deliberately minimal — `'\n\nEXAM REJECTED:\n' + details.join('\n')` and nothing else. The block's MEANING lives in examiner.md (per the global constraint that a new worker input is one labelled block spelled in the role file that reads it), so the engine adds no preamble sentence between the label and the first detail.

2. `examRounds` is set to 1 at the round-1 handoff call site, not inside `handoffExam()` — so the round-2 re-handoff cannot reset it, and the presence rule stays exactly `examEdited`'s.

3. `examEdited` is NOT reset by the round-2 handoff. A pre-review fix round's edit of the exam happened, and the record keeps it; `examEditedDiffs()` then renders an empty diff for that path in round 2's prompt, which is honest (the bytes are back to the peer's).

4. A round-2 examiner that throws is caught rather than allowed to climb: the implementation is finished and captured, and a whole-pair retry via runTask would throw it away to re-earn a finding the run already has. It reads as a BLOCKED round — the exam stands, round 2 runs.

5. `report-format.md`'s `tasks[].stateExams` row said this engine writes no numbered pass above `0`, which my change makes false (the exam-rejected round writes pass `2`). Corrected in the same edit: a `2` directory is now the exam-rejected round's re-execution, and the highest-numbered rule finding it rather than `0` is right — it is the last record the task's own tree produced.

6. `defaultTaskIdOf` already reads `T1` off `exam:T1:2` (`/^(?:exam|impl|fix):([^:]+)/`), so `cwdFor` resolves the exam clone with no change to run-waves.mjs.
